slides.title: Few-shot & negative examples
slides.lead: Show the model what good looks like.

slides.title: Few-shot prompting gives the model examples to learn from.
slides.lead: Instead of only describing what you want, provide one or more examples of the desired output.

body.introduction: The model can use them to infer patterns such as:

cards.title: Instruction only
cards.text: Summarise this claims update for senior management.

cards.title: With an example
cards.text:
Summarise this claims update for senior management.
Use the example below as a reference for tone, structure and level of detail.

Example: [insert strong previous update]

slides.keyIdea: Examples reduce how much the model has to interpret.

aside.label: RELATED CONCEPT
aside.title: Zero-shot vs. few-shot
items: Few-shot: one or more examples are provided as guidance

slides.title: Negative examples show the model what to avoid.

pairs.definition: What should the output look like?
What should the output not look like?

example.label: Insurance example
example.intro: Imagine you regularly create management updates about claims performance.

cards.title: Positive example
cards.text:
Status: Claims volumes increased by 12%.
Impact: Processing time is temporarily above target.
Action: Additional capacity has been activated.

cards.title: Negative example
cards.text: We would like to provide an update regarding various developments that have taken place within claims operations over the past reporting period…

slides.keyIdea: You do not always need both. Add a negative example when avoiding a specific pattern matters.

slides.title: Tell the model what to learn from each example.

lines: Use the examples below as guidance for the new output.
promptTemplate.footnote: Do not copy the content of the examples. Use them only as guidance for how the new output should be written.

band.label: Use when
band.text: The desired quality is easier to demonstrate than to describe.

slides.title: Can examples make a vague instruction more precise?

scenario.label: Scenario
scenario.text: Severe weather has increased claims volumes. Management needs a short update.

startingPrompt.label: Starting prompt
startingPrompt.text: Turn these notes into a short update for senior management.

blocks.text: Recent severe weather events have led to an increase in claims volumes. The claims organisation is currently taking several actions to manage the situation. Additional capacity has been made available, and developments will continue to be monitored.

blocks.heading: Status — Attention required
blocks.text: Severe-weather claims increased volumes and processing times.

blocks.heading: Response
blocks.text: Additional external capacity has been activated.

blocks.heading: Customer impact
blocks.text: No change to current customer communication is required.

blocks.heading: Next watchpoint
blocks.text: Reassess processing times at the end of the week.

band.label: What changed?
band.text: More specific · more structured · more actionable

slides.title: Use examples to guide your own output.

steps.hint: For example: stakeholder update · meeting summary · decision note · internal announcement
Choose something that represents the quality you want.
Use it if there is a recurring pattern you want to avoid.

steps.text: Tell AI what to learn from the examples.

disclaimer.text: Keep all information generic. Do not enter personal, customer or confidential information.
disclaimer.rationale: Compliance-critical in an insurance context - must not be reduced to a 12pt footer.

slides.title: Did the examples give you more control?
slides.lead: Compare the result with what you would normally receive.
slides.question: What changed most?
